name: Connected Components (Weakly and Strongly Connected)
problem_statement: Partition all vertices into maximal groups such that every pair of vertices within a group is connected according to a declared connectivity definition: weak (undirected) connectivity, or strong (directed, mutual-reachability) connectivity.

normalization: Remove self-loops; they never change component membership.
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair to one edge.
When connectivity_mode=weakly_connected, treat every edge as undirected regardless of input direction.

problem_inputs.name: connectivity_mode
problem_inputs.description: Weak connectivity ignores edge direction; strong connectivity requires a directed path in both directions and is only meaningful (and may differ from weak) on a directed graph.

required_outputs.name: component_assignment
required_outputs.description: Component index assigned to every vertex.

required_outputs.name: component_sizes
required_outputs.description: Vertex count of each component, indexed by component number.

optional_outputs.name: largest_component_id
optional_outputs.description: Component number with the most vertices.

optional_outputs.name: largest_component_size
optional_outputs.description: Vertex count of the largest component.

solution_semantics.objective: Assign every vertex a component_assignment such that two vertices share a component index if and only if they are connected under connectivity_mode, and components are maximal.
solution_semantics.exactness: This problem is always solved exactly; component identity is a decidable equivalence relation with no approximate mode.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex belongs to exactly one component.
solution_semantics.ordering: Component indices are canonically numbered by ascending smallest-member vertex ID, so results are directly comparable across independent runs or implementations.

validation_rules: Two vertices share a component_assignment value if and only if they are connected under connectivity_mode in the normalized graph.
component_count equals the number of distinct values in component_assignment.
component_sizes[i] equals the number of vertices assigned to component i, and the entries sum to the total vertex count.
Component numbering follows the ascending-smallest-member-vertex-ID convention.
edge_cases: An isolated vertex forms its own singleton component.
An edgeless graph has every vertex in its own singleton component, so component_count equals the vertex count.
connectivity_mode=strongly_connected on a graph requested as an undirected projection degenerates to the same result as weakly_connected.
A self-loop does not merge a vertex with any other vertex.

correctness: component-assignment agreement with an exhaustive BFS/DFS (weak) or Tarjan/Kosaraju (strong) oracle on small/medium fixtures
